title: Operator retries a failed job and releases a stuck claim
description:
Two dead ends share one fix. A job in `failed` is terminal: nothing retries it.
A job stuck in `claimed` -- a worker that crashed mid-generation, see
auritus-294fa6 -- is worse, because `GET /jobs/claimable` correctly excludes
non-pending jobs, so neither a local worker nor the Batch fallback will ever
touch it again. Both states need a route back to `pending`.

This is P0 because it has already happened in production three times in one
session (auritus-294fa6), and the only recovery was hand-crafting a
`PUT /jobs/{hash}/failed` with an operator bearer token.

Distinct from forced regeneration: retry applies to jobs that never produced
audio, does not delete an S3 object, and may be safely automatic for stale
claims. Share the reset helper with the regenerate story; do not fork it.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Recovering failed and stuck jobs

  Scenario: Operator retries a failed job
    Given a job exists with status "failed" and an error message
    When the operator retries that content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"
    And the job has no error message
    And the job appears in the claimable list

  Scenario: Operator releases a claim held by a crashed worker
    Given a job exists with status "claimed" by "local:node-1"
    And the claim is older than the claim timeout
    When the operator releases that content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"
    And the job has no claim owner
    And the job appears in the claimable list

  Scenario: Releasing a claim that is still live is rejected
    Given a job exists with status "claimed" by "local:node-1"
    And the claim was renewed within the claim timeout
    When the operator releases that content hash
    Then the response is a conflict
    And the job is still claimed by "local:node-1"

  Scenario: Operator force-releases a live claim
    Given a job exists with status "claimed" by "local:node-1"
    And the claim was renewed within the claim timeout
    When the operator force-releases that content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"
```

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`**

- Route: `POST /admin/jobs/{hash}/retry` -> `_retry_admin_job(content_hash, body, headers)`.
  One route covers both cases; the stored status decides the guard.
- `_retry_admin_job`:
  - `_require_operator(headers)`; load item or `LookupError`.
  - `status == "failed"` -> reset unconditionally.
  - `status == "claimed"` -> reset only when the claim is stale
    (`claimed_at` older than the claim timeout already used by
    `_claim_job`; reuse that constant, do not redefine it) or when
    `body.get("force") is True`. Otherwise raise the conflict error.
  - `status in ("pending", "done")` -> conflict; `done` belongs to regenerate.
  - Reset via the shared helper introduced by the regenerate story:
    `_reset_job_to_pending(content_hash, item, drop_audio=False)`. It clears
    claim and failure attributes and issues a fresh job token; `drop_audio`
    controls the S3 delete so regenerate passes `True` and retry passes `False`.
  - Re-arm the fallback via `_arm_fallback`.

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** — `def retry_job(self, content_hash: str, *, force: bool = False)`.

**`features/job_management.feature`** — extend with the scenarios above.

## Relationship to auritus-294fa6

That bug fixes the *cause* (the worker should mark its own job failed on any
exception before exiting). This story provides the *cure* for jobs already
orphaned, and for any future crash that escapes the worker's handler -- a
`kill -9` will always be able to orphan a claim. Both are needed. Land 294fa6's
worker fix independently; it does not block this story.
